findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher never checks the grant shortcut (inverted condition + wrong indices)
findings.body: The new matcher is supposed to verify that an access-token ID looks like `<sessionType><tokenType><grantType>:<uuid>` and that the grant part equals `expectedGrantShortcut`. Two defects make it a no-op: (1) the condition is inverted – `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` fails when the shortcut matches and passes when it does not; (2) the offsets are wrong – the encoded prefix is 6 chars with the grant shortcut at indices 4-6 (`substring(4, 6)`), while `substring(3, 5)` reads one char of the token-type and one of the grant-type. For the real value "onrtac" the extracted text is "ta", never equal to e.g. "ac", so the check always falls through to the UUID assertion. As a result all the converted assertions (`expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectAuthReqIdToToken`) silently accept any grant shortcut and the feature introduced by this PR is effectively untested.

findings.title: New abstract method getShortcut() on public SPI interface breaks existing grant-type providers
findings.body: `getShortcut()` is added to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` without a `default` implementation. Any third-party/custom OAuth2 grant type provider compiled against a previous version will no longer compile, and an already-deployed jar will fail at runtime with `AbstractMethodError` as soon as `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` iterates all grant factories and calls `getShortcut()`, which happens during server startup. Consider providing a `default` implementation (e.g. derived from the id, or returning null handled gracefully) to keep the SPI backwards compatible.

findings.title: postInit() can fail with NPE and silently accepts colliding shortcuts registered later
findings.body: In `postInit()` the shortcut returned by a grant factory is put directly into a `ConcurrentHashMap`. A custom (or future) factory returning `null` from `getShortcut()` makes `grantsByShortcuts.put(null, grantName)` throw a `NullPointerException`, aborting server startup with an obscure error instead of a meaningful validation message. In addition, the duplicate-shortcut validation (size comparison) runs only in `postInit()`; the lazy refresh paths `getShortcutByGrantType()`/`getGrantTypeByShortcut()` (lines 106-137) overwrite existing entries without any duplicate check, so a dynamically deployed grant reusing an existing shortcut would silently corrupt the mapping and make token IDs decode to the wrong grant type. The two maps are also updated with two independent `put` calls, so a concurrent reader can observe one map updated and the other not.

findings.title: Null check for rawTokenId actually re-checks grantType
findings.body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks `grantType` twice and never validates `rawTokenId`. A null `rawTokenId` therefore passes construction and later produces an encoded token id ending in the literal string "null" (`onrtac:null`), i.e. a corrupt `jti`, instead of failing fast at the point of the programming error. Should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

findings.title: Access tokens issued for offline_access are encoded with session type "on" (online)
findings.body: `createTokenResponse()` creates the access token (and thus the encoded session type) before `responseBuilder.generateRefreshToken()` converts/creates the offline session, and before the online user session is removed a few lines below (`session.sessions().removeUserSession(realm, userSession)` when the refresh token is of type offline). At the time `initToken()` runs, `userSession.isOffline()` is still false, so an access token obtained together with an offline refresh token gets the `on` (online) session-type prefix even though no online session exists afterwards. The same ordering exists in `ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType`. Since the stated purpose of the encoding is to let endpoints look up only the session type recorded in the token, this will lead to failed/incorrect session lookups for offline tokens once consumers rely on the value.

findings.title: Removal of Context copy constructor and new hard dependency on non-null formParams
findings.body: The public copy constructor `Context(Context context)` is removed from this server-spi-private class; any subclass or extension code that used it (e.g. to wrap/derive a grant context) will no longer compile. At the same time the remaining constructor now dereferences `formParams` (`formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`), so callers that previously could pass `null` form params now get a `NullPointerException`. If the copy constructor must go, the change should be noted as a breaking SPI change, and the constructor should tolerate a null `formParams`.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes because of an unrelated NullPointerException
findings.body: The test feeds the id "ofrtac:5678" whose shortcut "ac" is not in the hand-built map, so `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getGrantTypeByShortcut()` falls into the lazy-refresh branch and dereferences `sessionFactory`, which is `null` because `postInit()` was never called in the test. The thrown `NullPointerException` is swallowed by `catch (RuntimeException iae)`, so the test is green while the intended `IllegalArgumentException("Unknown value ... for grant type")` path is never exercised. The assertion should be narrowed to `IllegalArgumentException` (and the factory properly initialised), otherwise a regression in the error handling would go unnoticed.
